lem-finite-population-permutation-clt.claim: conditional convergence of the centered random-subset statistic to the standard normal
lem-finite-population-permutation-clt.empty: Statement restricts the tail to N>1 and 1<=m_N,n_N<=N-1; the subset sum has m_N terms and the empirical variance has N terms, so neither is empty.
lem-finite-population-permutation-clt.one: Statement permits m_N=1 at a finite row but m_N/N tends to p>0 and n_N/N tends to 1-p>0, so both sizes eventually exceed one; N=1 is explicitly removed.
lem-finite-population-permutation-clt.endpoints: Statement takes p strictly between 0 and 1; p=0 or p=1 would destroy the proportional denominator used in step 1.2.
lem-finite-population-permutation-clt.nonempty-choice: Statement and A1 assume AC for the martingale CLT and conditional-expectation interfaces; step 6.1 uses that supplier, so the former denial of choice was false.
lem-finite-population-permutation-clt.degenerate: Statement defines T_N=0 on S_N^2=0; step 4.1 proves this event is negligible because S_N^2 tends to sigma^2>0. A zero limiting variance is excluded.

lem-random-permutation-variance-by-trans.claim: the successive-revelation permutation variance upper bound
lem-random-permutation-variance-by-trans.empty: Statement has N>=1; at k=N the inner index set {N} remains nonempty. An empty revealed prefix at k=1 is allowed and its conditional average is M_0=Ef in step 1.1.

lem-permutation-mixture-coupling-for-two.claim: L2 negligibility of the aligned triangular-mixture coupling error
lem-permutation-mixture-coupling-for-two.empty: Statement inherits m,n>=r>=1 and eventually proportional sizes; in step 1.1 the mismatch set J can be empty when B_N=m, in which case the aligned rows agree and f=0.
lem-permutation-mixture-coupling-for-two.one: Statement allows r=1, for which M=mn and the same term-count bounds in step 3.1 hold; m=1 or n=1 cannot persist under proportional growth.
lem-permutation-mixture-coupling-for-two.endpoints: Statement assumes p in (0,1), ensuring m,n are both of order N in step 1.2; no p=0 or p=1 coupling limit is asserted.

def-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic.claim: the standard-error ratio S and its recomputed permutation law
def-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic.empty: Definition inherits m,n>=r>=1, making both binomial subset families nonempty; an empty group cannot supply the displayed divisions by m and n.
def-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic.one: Definition permits r=m=n=1 if nonnegative measurable variance routines are supplied; it uses those routines rather than requiring unbiased sample variances.
def-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic.endpoints: Definition takes nonnegative variance estimates, including zero; its piecewise S=0 branch covers a zero standard error without requiring a limiting mixture fraction.

thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.empty: Statement uses fixed r>=1 and m,n>=r; its U-statistic subset families are nonempty. Step 1.1 expands over all 2^(2r) mixed assignments, a nonempty finite collection, even when some mixture terms have zero values.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.one: Statement allows r=1; step 1.2 then expresses the projection as the centered sum over the uniformly chosen m-subset. A fixed m=1 cannot persist because m/N tends to p>0.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.endpoints: Statement restricts p to (0,1), making tau_p^2=r^2*sigma_p^2/(1-p) finite and positive. Step 2.1 divides only on the event S_g,N^2>0 and separately handles its complement.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.nonempty-choice: Statement assumes AC and its A1 identifies the finite-population conditional CLT F5 as the inherited use; step 2.1 explicitly applies F5 under A1.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.degenerate: Statement assumes sigma_p^2>0. Step 1.2 proves S_g,N^2 tends to this positive value and step 2.1 disposes of the empirical zero-variance event; a zero pooled limit is not covered.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.zero: Statement allows theta=0 as the weak null; step 2.1 sets the finite-population standardized numerator to zero when its empirical variance vanishes and proves that event negligible.

thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.claim: the all-assignment-centered specialization of the permutation CLT
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.empty: Statement imposes moment and zero-mean conditions for every P/Q argument assignment, a finite set with 2^(2r) members for r>=1. Step 1.1 applies the weak-null supplier to the nonempty inherited U-subset families.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.one: Statement permits the order-one case r=1, for which all four two-position P/Q assignments must be centered. Step 1.1 retains these hypotheses when invoking the general weak-null result.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.endpoints: Statement specifies p in (0,1); step 2.1 inherits exactly the scale r^2*sigma_p^2/(1-p) from F1, rather than a formula at either endpoint proportion.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.nonempty-choice: Statement explicitly assumes AC. A1 and step 2.1 inherit that assumption through the general weak-null permutation theorem F1, even though this specialization proof is only an implication check.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.degenerate: Statement keeps sigma_p^2>0 as an explicit premise; the additional assignment-wise zero means checked in step 1.1 do not replace or imply that premise.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-permutation-c.zero: Statement allows theta=0 as the weak null; step 2.1 sets the finite-population standardized numerator to zero when its empirical variance vanishes and proves that event negligible.

thm-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic-p.claim: both studentized normal limits with explicit permutation-consistency hypotheses
thm-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic-p.empty: Statement recomputes two nonnegative estimators from groups with m,n>=r>=1; neither group is empty. Step 1.1 takes a union of the two estimator failure events, which may individually be empty and then have probability zero.
thm-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic-p.one: Statement includes r=1 and requires actual supplied measurable variance routines; it does not demand a k-1 sample-variance formula at singleton k. The proportional asymptotic tail has both sizes diverging.
thm-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic-p.endpoints: Statement has p in (0,1); step 1.2 proves the rescaled standard error tends to the strictly positive tau_p, so step 2.1 chooses delta<tau_p/2 and never divides by an endpoint zero scale.
thm-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic-p.nonempty-choice: Statement assumes AC for F1 through F3: the permutation CLT, single-group contiguity transfer and true-sampling projection CLT. Step 1.1 uses A1 for transfer and step 3.1 for the sampling limit.
thm-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic-p.degenerate: Statement requires direct and pooled variances positive. Step 1.2 makes zero permuted standard errors negligible and step 3.1 does the same for the original denominator; the finite zero-ratio convention is retained.
thm-studentized-two-sample-u-statistic-p.zero: Statement allows theta=0 as the weak null; step 2.1 sets the finite-population standardized numerator to zero when its empirical variance vanishes and proves that event negligible.

thm-studentized-permutation-validity-und.claim: both studentized normal limits on the all-assignment-centered branch
thm-studentized-permutation-validity-und.empty: Statement imports the mixed-centered sample contract and the studentized statistic, whose two kernel subset families are nonempty. Step 1.1 checks the complete inherited hypotheses before applying the general studentized supplier.
thm-studentized-permutation-validity-und.one: Statement permits r=1 via the mixed-centered supplier; the two supplied estimators still require their own direct and conditional permutation consistency, as step 1.1 explicitly checks.
thm-studentized-permutation-validity-und.endpoints: Statement inherits proportional growth with an interior p from its mixed-centering theorem. Step 2.1 preserves the general studentized supplier scales and grants no endpoint-proportion extension.
thm-studentized-permutation-validity-und.nonempty-choice: Statement starts with AC and A1 inherits it through the general studentized theorem F1. Step 2.1 applies F1 under A1, so this branch does not remove the supplier choice assumption.
thm-studentized-permutation-validity-und.degenerate: Statement independently requires positive sigma_X^2, sigma_Y^2 and sigma_p^2; step 1.1 matches them to F1. Assignment-wise mean-zero assumptions alone do not ensure these nonzero variances.
thm-studentized-permutation-validity-und.zero: Statement allows theta=0 as the weak null; step 2.1 sets the finite-population standardized numerator to zero when its empirical variance vanishes and proves that event negligible.

ex-same-mean-unequal-variance-studentize.claim: a mean-difference example with raw variances 5/3 versus 7/3 and a calibrated studentized pivot
ex-same-mean-unequal-variance-studentize.empty: Example uses two nonempty IID groups, with m/N tending to 1/4; step 1.2 uses sample variances only for k>=2, which holds on the asymptotic tail.
ex-same-mean-unequal-variance-studentize.one: Example has r=1, so U is the difference of sample means; the k-1 sample-variance formula requires k>=2, as step 1.2 specifies.
ex-same-mean-unequal-variance-studentize.endpoints: Example fixes p=1/4 and step 4.1 takes alpha in (0,1); neither an empty group proportion nor alpha at 0 or 1 is part of its strict conservative-test comparison.
ex-same-mean-unequal-variance-studentize.nonempty-choice: Example and A1 assume AC for the sampling and permutation limit suppliers used in steps 3.1 and 4.1.
ex-same-mean-unequal-variance-studentize.degenerate: Example computes direct variances 1 and 2 and pooled variance 7/4 in steps 1.1 and 2.1, so all limiting scales are strictly positive.
ex-same-mean-unequal-variance-studentize.zero: Example gives mass 1/2 to zero under Q and both means zero; step 1.1 verifies theta=0 while step 1.2 proves the variance estimates approach positive values.

ex-exact-versus-weak-two-sample-null.claim: two concrete mean-null law pairs distinguishing finite exactness from asymptotic calibration
ex-exact-versus-weak-two-sample-null.empty: Example needs m,n>=2 for the sample-variance denominators; m/N tends to 1/2, so the finite asymptotic tail has nonempty training groups and nonempty variance sums.
ex-exact-versus-weak-two-sample-null.one: Example uses order r=1 but the k-1 variance estimate is evaluated for k>=2 on the asymptotic tail; it does not define that estimator for k=1.
ex-exact-versus-weak-two-sample-null.endpoints: Example fixes the limiting fraction 1/2, so there is no endpoint proportion to evaluate; finite zero standard errors use the inherited ratio convention.
ex-exact-versus-weak-two-sample-null.nonempty-choice: Example A1 assumes AC for the asymptotic result used in step 2.1; the finite invariance comparison in step 1.2 uses finite group ranks.
ex-exact-versus-weak-two-sample-null.zero: Example has theta=0 in both pairs, with Q assigning mass 1/2 to zero only in the heterogeneous pair; step 1.2 uses that event to witness P!=Q.

ex-studentized-rank-u-statistic-under-we.claim: the finite-support sign-rank example with joint projection-variance estimates
ex-studentized-rank-u-statistic-under-we.empty: Example has m,n growing with m/N tending to 1/2; every row/column mean averages at least one observation, and the variance denominators are used on the tail m,n>=2.
ex-studentized-rank-u-statistic-under-we.one: Example sets r=1 and uses all mn sign comparisons; its sample variances need m,n>=2 on the asymptotic tail rather than a one-observation variance estimate.
ex-studentized-rank-u-statistic-under-we.endpoints: Example fixes p=1/2; the estimator factors m/(m-1), n/(n-1) are used only once sizes exceed one, as in step 2.2.
ex-studentized-rank-u-statistic-under-we.nonempty-choice: Example A1 assumes AC for the permutation transfer and normal-limit result, used explicitly in step 2.2 and step 3.1.
ex-studentized-rank-u-statistic-under-we.degenerate: Example steps 1.1 and 1.2 compute sigma_X^2=1/4, sigma_Y^2=1/2 and pooled variance 81/256, excluding a degenerate limiting projection.
ex-studentized-rank-u-statistic-under-we.zero: Example has g_Y(1)=0 and pooled g(1)=0, yet the other support values give positive variances; step 1.1 separately verifies theta=0.

lem-moving-block-bootstrap-conditional-c.claim: the exact full-plus-prefix moving-block covariance identity
lem-moving-block-bootstrap-conditional-c.empty: Statement has n>=b>=1 and N=n-b+1>=1; the prefix r=0 is the permitted empty sum and is assigned C_0=0, so step 1.1 omits that contribution.
lem-moving-block-bootstrap-conditional-c.zero: Statement sets C_0=0; when all observed x_t are zero, every S_j and C_q vanishes and step 2.1 gives zero on both sides.
lem-moving-block-bootstrap-conditional-c.degenerate: Statement permits identical candidate block sums, so C_b or C_r may be zero; step 2.1 adds these zero covariances without any positivity division.
lem-moving-block-bootstrap-conditional-c.endpoints: Statement allows b=1 and b=n. For b=n, N=k=1 and r=0, so the sole candidate block is deterministic and C_b=0.
lem-moving-block-bootstrap-conditional-c.nonempty-choice: Statement samples only finitely many independent uniform starts from {1,...,N}; step 1.1 expands a finite product law and uses no arbitrary choice function.

lem-tapered-block-bootstrap-conditional-.claim: the exact full-plus-prefix tapered covariance identity
lem-tapered-block-bootstrap-conditional-.empty: Statement has N=n-b+1>=1 and sets V_0=0 for the empty prefix r=0; the complete blocks remain nonempty because 1<=b<=n.
lem-tapered-block-bootstrap-conditional-.zero: Statement retains W_b>0, but all observations may be zero; then R_t=T_j^(q)=0 and step 2.1 yields zero covariance.
lem-tapered-block-bootstrap-conditional-.degenerate: Statement permits every tapered candidate sum to coincide; then its V_q is zero, and covariance additivity in step 2.1 still applies.
lem-tapered-block-bootstrap-conditional-.endpoints: Statement permits b=n with W_b>0: N=k=1 and r=0, hence each candidate covariance V_q is zero and the bootstrap mean is deterministic.
lem-tapered-block-bootstrap-conditional-.nonempty-choice: Statement uses the finite independent uniform-start law of the algorithm; step 1.1 only averages finitely many tapered candidates, without an arbitrary-index choice.

lem-taper-window-l2-normalization.claim: midpoint squared-window normalization and positivity of its limiting integral
lem-taper-window-l2-normalization.empty: Statement uses b>=1, so the weight vector is nonempty; the window is positive near 1/2, and step 1.2 supplies a nonempty central interval giving I_w>0.

lem-k-sample-null-centering.claim: the pooled conditional mean of every retained pseudo-observation
lem-k-sample-null-centering.empty: Statement inherits K>=2, n_i>=1, b_i>=1 and N_i>=1; a truncated final block retains q>=1 positions, and no extra empty block is appended in the divisible case.
lem-k-sample-null-centering.zero: Statement allows pooled mean zero; subtracting c_i,r makes each candidate offset have expectation zero in step 1.1, so each series mean then also has expectation zero.
lem-k-sample-null-centering.degenerate: Statement permits all observations in a series to coincide; every residual candidate is then zero and its pseudo-series equals the pooled mean deterministically.
lem-k-sample-null-centering.one: Statement permits n_i=b_i=1, giving N_i=k_i=1 and zero residual; that singleton series is the one-entry pseudo-series consisting of the pooled mean.
lem-k-sample-null-centering.endpoints: Statement covers both moving and tapered modes and b_i=n_i: one candidate remains and position centering removes every random residual.
lem-k-sample-null-centering.nonempty-choice: Statement requires only the finite product of independent uniform starts across fixed K series; step 1.1 computes each expectation by a finite sum.

thm-conditional-bootstrap-hadamard-delta.claim: the conditional delta conclusion for a continuous linear tangential derivative
thm-conditional-bootstrap-hadamard-delta.empty: Statement has theta in a neighbourhood D, so D is nonempty; E_0 is a linear subspace and contains zero. Step 3.1 permits an empty closed test set, for which the probability inequality is 0<=0.
thm-conditional-bootstrap-hadamard-delta.zero: Statement permits derivative Psi_prime=0 or G=0; step 3.1 then gives the point-mass output law at zero. The quotient never takes t_n=0 because t_n>0.
thm-conditional-bootstrap-hadamard-delta.one: Statement permits one-dimensional E and F, but its sequence index still tends to infinity; step 1.1 also works for a singleton compact direction set.

thm-k-sample-block-bootstrap-validity.claim: continuous contrasts of explicitly supplied joint sampling and bootstrap limits
thm-k-sample-block-bootstrap-validity.empty: Statement fixes K>=2 and n_i>=b_i>=1; the contrast has K-1>=1 coordinates. Step 2.2 allows the empty closed test set and its probability is zero.
thm-k-sample-block-bootstrap-validity.zero: Statement permits the common mean mu=0 and a zero Gaussian contrast; step 1.1 cancels the common locations, without dividing by their values.
thm-k-sample-block-bootstrap-validity.degenerate: Statement imposes no positive variance on G_i or on the contrast; continuous mapping in step 3.1 applies to a point mass as well as a nondegenerate limit.
thm-k-sample-block-bootstrap-validity.one: Statement excludes K=1 because contrasts require K>=2, while finite n_i=1 is allowed if b_i=1. The positive limiting theta_i forces every series size to diverge.

ex-moving-block-bootstrap-small-sample.claim: the explicit resampling of 0,1,2,3 in blocks of length two
ex-moving-block-bootstrap-small-sample.empty: Example has n=4, b=2 and exactly three candidate blocks; the remainder r=0 is empty and no third selected block is used.
ex-moving-block-bootstrap-small-sample.zero: Example includes the observation zero in candidate (0,1), which is retained as an ordinary value; step 1.1 still gives position expectations 1 and 2.
ex-moving-block-bootstrap-small-sample.degenerate: Example has three distinct blocks, so each start is random; the conditional sample mean takes values 1/2,1,3/2,2,5/2 and is not deterministic.
ex-moving-block-bootstrap-small-sample.one: Example uses unit scalar observations but fixes n=4 and b=2; the one-start event J_s=1 selects (0,1), one of three equiprobable blocks.
ex-moving-block-bootstrap-small-sample.endpoints: Example candidate starts are 1,2,3; start 3 selects (2,3) and ends exactly at the fourth observation, with no wraparound.
ex-moving-block-bootstrap-small-sample.nonempty-choice: Example enumerates a finite three-point start set twice independently; the explicit averages in step 1.1 require no choice principle.

ex-tapered-block-bootstrap-triangular-wi.claim: the three midpoint triangular weights and their exact L2 scaling
ex-tapered-block-bootstrap-triangular-wi.empty: Example fixes the nonempty weight vector (1/3,1,1/3); its squared norm is 11/9 in step 1.1, so the normalization denominator is nonzero.
ex-tapered-block-bootstrap-triangular-wi.zero: Example window vanishes at u=0 and u=1, while all three midpoint weights are positive; step 1.1 therefore never divides by zero.
ex-tapered-block-bootstrap-triangular-wi.degenerate: Example gives W_3^2=11/9>0 and scaled squared sum 3; a zero taper is excluded by these actual computed values.
ex-tapered-block-bootstrap-triangular-wi.one: Example includes the central midpoint weight w(1/2)=1; step 1.1 scales it to 3*sqrt(3/11), distinct from the two outer weights.
ex-tapered-block-bootstrap-triangular-wi.nonempty-choice: Example evaluates a fixed polynomial-piecewise formula at three prescribed points and performs finite arithmetic in steps 1.1 and 2.1; no selection from a family is used.

cex-pointwise-bootstrap-ar1-variance-mis.claim: failure of pointwise-bootstrap variance consistency for the stationary AR(1) filter
cex-pointwise-bootstrap-ar1-variance-mis.empty: Statement refuted uses n>=1 empirical draws; the Counterexample uses the infinite geometric filter with nonempty j>=0 terms. At n=1 the positive-lag covariance sum is empty and contributes zero in step 5.1.

def-two-sample-u-statistic-parameter.one: Definition allows r=1: each symmetry requirement on a one-coordinate block is automatic and theta is the ordinary P-times-Q integral.
def-two-sample-u-statistic-parameter.degenerate: Definition allows point-mass P or Q and a constant kernel, giving its finite constant expectation; no projection-variance positivity is imposed.
def-two-sample-u-statistic-parameter.empty: Definition has r>=1 and probability measures P,Q, so the underlying measurable space cannot be empty; there is no empty product block.
def-two-sample-u-statistic-parameter.endpoints: Definition permits the smallest order r=1 and any integrable real kernel; it introduces no mixture fraction or alpha parameter with additional endpoints.
def-two-sample-u-statistic-parameter.zero: Definition permits h=0 and theta=0, but neither is required; integrability supplies a finite real value without imposing a null.
def-two-sample-u-statistic-parameter.nonempty-choice: Definition uses supplied probability measures and their fixed finite product of 2r factors; no arbitrary family of witnesses is selected.

lem-hypergeometric-binomial-contiguity-f.claim: one-way transfer of vanishing count probabilities by a mean-one likelihood-ratio limit
lem-hypergeometric-binomial-contiguity-f.one: Statement permits finite rows with a single marked object or a single draw, but p_N->p and k_N/N->s with p,s in (0,1) force all relevant counts to grow on the tail.
lem-hypergeometric-binomial-contiguity-f.degenerate: Statement excludes p or s at 0 or 1; step 3.1 has variance k_N p_N(1-p_N) of order N, which is not a degenerate CLT normalization.
lem-hypergeometric-binomial-contiguity-f.empty: Statement quantifies over sets A_N, including A_N=empty; step 7.1 then gives both count probabilities zero. Sampling sizes and marked/unmarked populations are positive on the tail.
lem-hypergeometric-binomial-contiguity-f.endpoints: Statement restricts limiting p,s to (0,1); the likelihood-ratio prefactor (1-s)^(-1/2) has no asserted s=1 extension.

lem-general-measurable-finite-group-rand.claim: superuniform inclusive ranks and uniform randomized ranks under a measurable invariant action
lem-general-measurable-finite-group-rand.one: Statement permits the one-element group {e}; its inclusive p-value is 1 and its randomized p-value equals U, as the formulas directly show.
lem-general-measurable-finite-group-rand.degenerate: Statement permits constant T or an action with a singleton orbit: all ranks tie, so p_0=1 and p_U=U; step 1.1 retains multiplicity in the finite list.
lem-general-measurable-finite-group-rand.endpoints: Statement allows U=0 and U=1 in the rank formula, producing the ends of a tie interval; the uniform randomizer hits either endpoint with probability zero.
lem-general-measurable-finite-group-rand.zero: Statement permits T=0 everywhere; every group element ties and p_U=U while p_0=1, so zero score is not a zero denominator.
lem-general-measurable-finite-group-rand.nonempty-choice: Statement has a supplied finite group and step 2.1 expressly uses finite ranks and averages without a choice axiom; no family of representatives is selected.

def-two-sample-order-r-u-statistic-and-f.claim: the finite kernel average and centered L2 first projections
def-two-sample-order-r-u-statistic-and-f.one: Definition permits r=1 and m=n=1; the average then has one kernel term and its projection formulas integrate the other single coordinate.
def-two-sample-order-r-u-statistic-and-f.degenerate: Definition permits zero first projections and constant kernels; the projections are centered L2 classes, without a nonzero variance condition.
def-two-sample-order-r-u-statistic-and-f.empty: Definition has m,n>=r>=1, so the subset families are nonempty. For r=1 the unretained part of its own block has zero coordinates and its product integral is the scalar identity.
def-two-sample-order-r-u-statistic-and-f.zero: Definition admits h=0 or theta=0; for h=0 the U-statistic and both centered projections vanish.
def-two-sample-order-r-u-statistic-and-f.nonempty-choice: Definition uses increasing index order for selected subsets and treats projections as almost-everywhere classes; no arbitrary representatives across an indexed family are selected.

lem-permutation-consistency-from-iid-mix.claim: transfer of a single-group triangular-mixture consistency assumption to a permuted group
lem-permutation-consistency-from-iid-mix.one: Statement concerns either group size m_N or n_N; each tends to infinity under the interior limiting fraction, so a fixed singleton group cannot be its asymptotic regime.
lem-permutation-consistency-from-iid-mix.degenerate: Statement permits P=Q or a constant statistic T_N=c_N; then both IID-mixture and permutation failure probabilities are exactly zero in step 1.2.
lem-permutation-consistency-from-iid-mix.empty: Statement includes failure events that may be empty; their f_N(j) is zero and steps 2.1–3.1 return zero. The sample groups themselves are nonempty on the proportional tail.

lem-two-sample-u-statistic-projections-w.claim: finite measurable centered L2 versions of the two section projections
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-projections-w.one: Statement includes r=1: section integration is over the other block only, and the Cauchy–Schwarz estimates in step 2.1 remain probability-space estimates.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-projections-w.degenerate: Statement permits h to be constant or zero; step 3.1 subtracts its mean and both projections then vanish.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-projections-w.empty: Statement inherits r>=1 and probability spaces, excluding an empty sample space. Its exceptional section null set may be empty, in which case step 1.2 changes no values.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-projections-w.endpoints: Statement includes the borderline h second moment zero, which forces h=0 almost everywhere and both projections zero; it requires only finiteness, not strict positivity.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-projections-w.nonempty-choice: Statement uses measurable section integrals with a prescribed zero value on exceptional null sets in step 1.2, so it does not choose arbitrary representatives.

lem-pooled-mixture-projection-and-varian.claim: zero pooled mean, opposite projections, and continuity of the pooled variance
lem-pooled-mixture-projection-and-varian.one: Statement includes r=1; its section expansion then has one remaining argument, and the scale limit still equals sigma_p^2/(1-p).
lem-pooled-mixture-projection-and-varian.degenerate: Statement permits sigma_t^2=0; step 1.2 proves finiteness and continuity without dividing by that variance, so the final limit may be zero.
lem-pooled-mixture-projection-and-varian.empty: Statement has r>=1, so there are 2r-1>=1 remaining coordinates; its finite mixed-assignment expansion has 2^(2r-1) terms and is never empty.
lem-pooled-mixture-projection-and-varian.endpoints: Statement restricts t and limiting p to (0,1); its displayed r^2/(1-p) scale is not extended to p=1.
lem-pooled-mixture-projection-and-varian.zero: Statement proves theta of the pooled law is exactly zero by antisymmetry in step 1.1, and allows g_t=0 and sigma_t^2=0.
lem-pooled-mixture-projection-and-varian.nonempty-choice: Statement uses finitely many mixed-assignment section functions; step 1.2 supplies one common measurable version by a fixed zero-on-null-set prescription, not an arbitrary family choice.

lem-two-sample-u-statistic-hoeffding-dec.claim: the finite coordinate-operator decomposition into canonical components
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-hoeffding-dec.one: Statement includes r=1; the two first-order terms and the (1,1) interaction exhaust the nonconstant expansion.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-hoeffding-dec.degenerate: Statement permits g_X=g_Y=0, leaving only higher canonical terms; the finite operator identity in step 2.1 does not require nonzero projections.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-hoeffding-dec.empty: Statement explicitly assigns the empty selected-coordinate component U_0,0=theta; step 2.1 identifies it, then removes it from U-theta.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-hoeffding-dec.endpoints: Statement includes a=0 or b=0 and a=r or b=r; integration over no selected coordinates gives theta, while Q operators are used on every retained coordinate at the upper endpoint.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-hoeffding-dec.nonempty-choice: Statement applies a fixed finite product expansion of 2r commuting operators; block symmetry removes dependence on which coordinate subset is used, so no arbitrary family choice is needed.

lem-two-sample-u-statistic-degenerate-re.claim: the uniform O(N^-2) second-moment bound for the canonical remainder
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-degenerate-re.one: Statement permits r=1; the remainder contains the single (a,b)=(1,1) term and its denominator mn has order N^2.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-degenerate-re.degenerate: Statement concerns canonical higher-order terms even when first projections vanish; step 2.1 still bounds their total variance and gives sqrt(N)R->0.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-degenerate-re.empty: Statement includes components with a=0 or b=0; step 1.1 uses binomial(m,0)=binomial(n,0)=1 for these empty index subsets, not a zero denominator.
lem-two-sample-u-statistic-degenerate-re.nonempty-choice: Statement works with finitely many pairs 0<=a,b<=r and finite subset sums; the canonical-coordinate integration in step 1.1 selects an index from a finite difference set only.

thm-two-sample-u-statistic-projection-cl.one: Statement permits r=1; step 1.1 then reduces to the two independent projection sums plus the negligible interaction remainder.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-projection-cl.degenerate: Statement requires both sigma_X^2 and sigma_Y^2 strictly positive; step 3.1 explicitly declines a claim when either is zero.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-projection-cl.empty: Statement inherits m,n>=r>=1 and proportional growth; no empty group average occurs, while individual projection sums can evaluate to zero without becoming empty.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-projection-cl.endpoints: Statement takes p in (0,1), making p/(1-p) positive finite; it provides no endpoint-proportion normal limit.
thm-two-sample-u-statistic-projection-cl.zero: Statement assumes theta=0, but positive direct projection variances make its limiting variance r^2*(sigma_X^2+p*sigma_Y^2/(1-p)) nonzero.

cor-two-sample-permutation-exact-under-e.claim: finite-sample orbit-rank validity when the two laws coincide
cor-two-sample-permutation-exact-under-e.one: Statement permits m=n=r=1 with supplied variance routines; the pooled permutation group still has two elements and the zero-denominator ratio remains a real statistic.
cor-two-sample-permutation-exact-under-e.degenerate: Statement requires no nondegenerate projection; if all scores coincide, inclusive rank is 1 and tie randomization returns U, consistent with step 3.1.
cor-two-sample-permutation-exact-under-e.endpoints: Statement uses the complete independent tie randomizer U on [0,1]; the endpoint rank values are included in its formula and have probability zero under uniform U.
cor-two-sample-permutation-exact-under-e.nonempty-choice: Statement uses a fixed finite symmetric group on N=m+n coordinates; step 1.1 checks rectangle products and step 3.1 applies finite ranks without arbitrary-index choice.

cex-weak-null-does-not-imply-mixed-assig.claim: the order-two product-difference witness with a nonzero mixed-assignment mean
cex-weak-null-does-not-imply-mixed-assig.one: Counterexample fixes r=2 rather than order one; its law weights 3/4 and 1/4 give means +1/2 and -1/2 in step 1.1.
cex-weak-null-does-not-imply-mixed-assig.degenerate: Counterexample step 1.4 computes both direct variances 3/16 and a positive pooled variance at p=1/4, so the failure of mixed centering is not caused by a zero projection.
cex-weak-null-does-not-imply-mixed-assig.empty: Counterexample evaluates exactly four independent arguments with r=2; each P or Q is a two-point probability law, and no empty argument block is used.
cex-weak-null-does-not-imply-mixed-assig.endpoints: Counterexample uses p=1/4 for its pooled variance and masses 1/4,3/4, all interior; no endpoint mixture is needed to refute the implication.
cex-weak-null-does-not-imply-mixed-assig.zero: Counterexample has theta=0 in step 1.1 but mixed mean 1/2 in step 1.2; zeros in the supports make kernel products zero with positive probability without nullifying their variances.
cex-weak-null-does-not-imply-mixed-assig.nonempty-choice: Counterexample uses explicit finite laws on {0,2} and {0,-2}; step 1.2 computes a four-factor product expectation, with no representative-selection principle.

cex-positive-kernel-second-moment-does-n.claim: the Rademacher order-two witness with positive kernel moment and zero first projections
cex-positive-kernel-second-moment-does-n.one: Counterexample fixes r=2; each argument takes one of two signs and step 1.2 uses products whose squares equal one.
cex-positive-kernel-second-moment-does-n.empty: Counterexample evaluates two coordinates in each block and uses nonempty Rademacher supports; in step 1.3 all section means vanish by centering, not by empty integration.
cex-positive-kernel-second-moment-does-n.endpoints: Counterexample has P=Q and fixed sign probabilities 1/2; any interior sample fraction in step 2.1 gives the same zero sqrt(m) limit.
cex-positive-kernel-second-moment-does-n.zero: Counterexample step 1.3 gives g_X=g_Y=0 and both projection variances zero, while step 1.2 gives E[h^2]=2; this is the actual failed implication.
cex-positive-kernel-second-moment-does-n.nonempty-choice: Counterexample has a prescribed four-coordinate Rademacher product law; all moment and section calculations in steps 1.1–1.3 are finite sums.

cex-extra-sqrt-m-after-standard-error-st.claim: escape from every bounded interval after multiplying the already-studentized Rademacher pivot by sqrt(m)
cex-extra-sqrt-m-after-standard-error-st.one: Counterexample has r=1, while each usual sample variance uses k>=2 on the proportional-growth tail; k=1 is not an estimator evaluation in its asymptotic argument.
cex-extra-sqrt-m-after-standard-error-st.degenerate: Counterexample step 1.1 gives direct and pooled variances one; failure of the extra scaling follows from a nondegenerate N(0,1) pivot, not a zero-variance limit.
cex-extra-sqrt-m-after-standard-error-st.empty: Counterexample uses two growing nonempty groups; the interval [-M,M] in step 2.1 is nonempty for M>0, and the argument shows its probability tends to zero.
cex-extra-sqrt-m-after-standard-error-st.endpoints: Counterexample assumes an interior sample fraction p; step 2.1 takes M>0 and then epsilon down to zero, with no assertion of an endpoint-proportion extension.
cex-extra-sqrt-m-after-standard-error-st.zero: Counterexample theta is zero and the inherited ratio is set to zero on a zero estimated error. Step 1.2 makes that exceptional event negligible through variance consistency to one.

ex-block-length-n-one-third.claim: admissibility and asymptotic rates of the ceiling cube-root block length
ex-block-length-n-one-third.nonempty-choice: Example defines b_n as the least integer >=n^(1/3); step 1.1 uses this unique ceiling value, with no arbitrary family selection.

ex-two-series-block-bootstrap-null-cente.claim: the explicit pooled-mean 58/7 construction with a retained final prefix
ex-two-series-block-bootstrap-null-cente.zero: Example step 1.1 produces a zero offset candidate (0,0) for the second series; it leaves the output at 58/7 and contributes zero to the offset expectation in step 2.1.
ex-two-series-block-bootstrap-null-cente.nonempty-choice: Example has two independent choices from {-1,1} and two from {-2,0,2} in step 2.1, all specified finite uniforms; no arbitrary witness family is used.

ex-iid-functional-data-block-bootstrap.claim: the IID signed constant-function instance of moving and tapered bootstrap
ex-iid-functional-data-block-bootstrap.zero: Example step 1.1 has EX_t=0 and delta_m=0 for every m>=1, though E||X_t||^2=1; zero replacement error satisfies both summability and the rate condition.
ex-iid-functional-data-block-bootstrap.nonempty-choice: Example explicitly assumes AC and step 2.1 invokes the two Hilbert bootstrap theorems under that assumption; the constant function and sign law are explicitly given.

lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-an.claim: uniform block moments and trace-norm convergence of normalized weighted overlapping covariance
lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-an.empty: Statement includes q=0: the prefix sum is empty and both moment bounds read 0<=0. For fixed h>=b the lag-weight sum is empty and equals zero; the fixed-h limit is taken only as b grows.

lem-conditional-independent-block-bootst.claim: the centered independent-block conditional CLT including its final prefix
lem-conditional-independent-block-bootst.empty: Statement explicitly sets B_j,0=bar B_0=C_0=0; r=0 therefore contributes an empty zero prefix. Candidate starts remain nonempty because n>=b on the admissible tail.
lem-conditional-independent-block-bootst.one: Statement includes b=1 at finite rows and a one-point start set if b=n, but neither can persist when b->infinity and b/sqrt(n)->0; the asymptotic number of complete blocks diverges.

thm-moving-block-bootstrap-clt-for-depen.claim: the admissible-tail moving-block Hilbert CLT and Hilbert–Schmidt covariance limit
thm-moving-block-bootstrap-clt-for-depen.empty: Statement applies only on the tail 1<=b_n<=n, so every candidate-start family is nonempty; if b_n divides n, the zero-length prefix in step 2.1 contributes zero.
thm-moving-block-bootstrap-clt-for-depen.one: Statement allows finite early b_n=1 but requires b_n->infinity, so singleton blocks are not its limiting regime; no assertion about fixed n=1 is made.

thm-tapered-block-bootstrap-clt-for-depe.claim: the admissible-tail tapered Hilbert CLT and Hilbert–Schmidt covariance limit
thm-tapered-block-bootstrap-clt-for-depe.empty: Statement applies only where 1<=b_n<=n and W_b>0; the candidate family is nonempty. Step 2.1 uses an empty zero prefix when b_n divides n.
thm-tapered-block-bootstrap-clt-for-depe.one: Statement permits early b=1 when W_1>0, but b_n->infinity excludes a fixed singleton-block asymptotic regime; the limit concerns only its admissible tail.

def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-prob.claim: conditional convergence defined by a supplied measurable weak-metric distance
def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-prob.empty: Definition supplies a Borel probability law on E, which prevents E being empty; no empirical-sample size restriction is needed to define that law.
def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-prob.one: Definition permits a singleton E; its only probability law has zero distance to itself, so every supplied conditional law satisfies the displayed convergence.
def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-prob.degenerate: Definition permits the fixed limit mu to be a point mass; weak convergence in its supplied metric remains the same criterion.
def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-prob.iff-forward: Definition requires the supplied metric to satisfy d_w(mu_n,mu)->0 implies mu_n weakly converges to mu; this is an explicit property of the supplied metric, not a metric-existence proof.
def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-prob.iff-reverse: Definition also requires mu_n weakly converging to mu to imply d_w(mu_n,mu)->0. The words exactly when expressly require this converse property.

lem-independent-tail-replacement-errors-.claim: the twice-residual identity, monotonicity and summability-implies-rate implication
lem-independent-tail-replacement-errors-.empty: Statement uses m>=1 retained innovations; in step 3.1 the tail index set {ceil(m/2),...,m} is nonempty for m>=2. The infinite residual tail may have zero error, but it is not an empty sample.
lem-independent-tail-replacement-errors-.degenerate: Statement allows X to be prefix-measurable: step 2.1 then gives delta_m=0 and g_m=X almost surely, preserving the minimization and all later zero errors.

alg-random-permutation-monte-carlo-pvalu.claim: the identity-corrected Monte Carlo p-value for two specified simulation designs
alg-random-permutation-monte-carlo-pvalu.empty: Definition expressly permits B=0: the with-replacement sum over b=1,...,B is empty and equals zero; without replacement S is the empty subset. Both designs retain {e} and return 1.

thm-studentized-wilcoxon-validity-under-.claim: studentized Wilcoxon sampling/permutation limits and the equal-law finite exactness specialization
thm-studentized-wilcoxon-validity-under-.empty: Statement has m,n>=2, so row, column and variance sums are nonempty; the no-tie event may be empty for atomic laws, and the tie-corrected kernel still gives h(x,x)=0 in step 1.1.

thm-cross-validation-risk-bias-at-traini.claim: the schedule-weighted training-size expectation and exact bias identity
thm-cross-validation-risk-bias-at-traini.empty: Statement inherits nonempty training and validation sets and weights summing to one; a schedule with B=0 cannot have that sum. Individual zero-weight splits are allowed and contribute zero in step 2.1.

lem-kfold-cv-variance-covariance-decompo.claim: the exact equal-fold covariance-class variance decomposition
lem-kfold-cv-variance-covariance-decompo.empty: Statement has K>=2 and m>=1, hence n>=2 and every fold and its training complement are nonempty. When m=1 the family of within-fold distinct pairs is empty; omega=0 and its count n(m-1)=0 in step 3.1.
